name: napalm-820a06b2-blind17-ots
instr:
# napalm: diagnosing a batch of undocumented regressions without a test suite

We automate a mixed fleet of routers and switches with this library, and after moving our tooling to a newer checkout a great deal of previously working behaviour is wrong. The repository has received 17 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about our gear, our credentials or our own scripts changed. Everything below is what I could pin down by observation, and where closely related behaviour still works I have said so.

Some of it goes wrong before any equipment is contacted. Asking for a vendor plug-in by its fully qualified, dotted, package-style name is refused as an unacceptable name, bundled and third-party alike, while a name with an extra dotted component on the end, which used to be rejected out of hand, is accepted — the decision looks turned inside out; plain undotted short names still resolve. The offline stand-in that replays canned replies saved on disk is unusable: read-only queries come back as though nothing had been recorded, asking deliberately for one with no recorded data no longer raises the expected not-implemented or no-data failure, the arrangement for making a recorded call report an equipment error on demand never fires, and passing arguments through is affected too. Turning a human-readable running-time string spelling out years, weeks, days, hours and minutes into a number of seconds is off by orders of magnitude, the units no longer told apart.
